newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dredging upturn seen buoying Boskalis H1.
newsitem.headline: Dredging upturn seen buoying Boskalis H1.

text.p: Dredger Boskalis is seen posting double-digit profit growth in the first half of 1997 on Thursday, buoyed by the upturn in world dredging markets.
Analysts expect the Papendrecht-based company to report first-half net from ordinary operations of between 29 and 38 million guilders on Thursday.
Consensus stands at 33 million guilders, up from the 27 million guilders achieved a year ago.
"Fleet capacity utilisation is rising, with major projects coming onto the market worldwide," said Rene van Geffen of Van Lanschot Bankiers.

"Add to that the fact that the west European construction industry was not hampered by a strong winter this year as it was last year and the stage is set for a rise in first-half earnings to 34 million," he said.
Labouchere's construction analyst Sven Smit is slightly more cautious, forecasting first-half net from ordinary operations will rise by some 11 percent to 30.6 million guilders.

"The company itself has indicated that the biggest impact of the growth in orders will be seen in the second half," he said, adding this could yield a 37 percent jump in year-on-year profits to 47 million guilders.
By contrast, profit growth in the first half will have been braked by a number of low-margin projects, he believes.
Analysts are agreed that the medium-term outlook for the dredging industry is bright, with new orders more than able to offset the worldwide rise in fleet capacity over the next two to three years.
Van Geffen points to rising demand in South East Asia, central and Latin America, and western Europe.
"Singapore should generate several hundreds of millions of guilders in orders, while Hong Kong demand is set to pick up again after a relatively quiet period," Smit says.
However, from 1999 overcapacity could again become a significant factor, pulling margins and profits down, analysts caution.
